    70	/-!
    71	The paper fixes the field representation and self-dual normal basis once for
    72	each admissible field size.  We expose that choice through a single global
    73	selector rather than carrying a potentially different model in every game
    74	parameter record.  Existence is a named stage-4.3 proof obligation; the
    75	selector itself is the resulting noncomputable choice.
    76	-/
    77	
    78	/-- An admissible binary field size admits the fixed self-dual normal model used
    79	by the Pauli basis test.  This is the existence assertion implicit in
    80	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis` and `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:234-246,298-315`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680,702-725`.
    83	
    84	The construction of the basis and its natural coding is deferred to the
    85	algebra stage; keeping it as a named theorem makes the proof obligation visible
    86	without adding a model hypothesis to the source-facing test statements.
    87	-/
    88	theorem exists_fixed_field_model (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    89	    Nonempty (FixedFieldModel q) := by
    90	  sorry
    91	
    92	/-- The once-and-for-all field model selected for an admissible size.  Every
    93	QPBT parameter record uses this same choice, matching the paper's fixed
    94	self-dual normal-basis identification rather than quantifying over arbitrary
    95	representations.  Blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`; paper origin
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`.
    97	-/
    98	noncomputable def fixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    99	    FixedFieldModel q :=
   100	  Classical.choice (exists_fixed_field_model q hq)
   101	
   102	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Field F.K := F.toFieldModel.instField
   103	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Fintype F.K := F.toFieldModel.instFintype
   104	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : DecidableEq F.K := F.toFieldModel.instDecidableEq
   105	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Algebra (ZMod 2) F.K := F.algebra
   106	
   107	/-- The fixed binary representation obtained from the chosen basis coordinates. -/
   108	noncomputable def binaryRepresentation {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K ≃ Fin q :=
   109	  F.toFieldModel.equiv
   110	
   111	/--
   112	The coordinate map associated with a finite basis.  This is the `κ` of
   113	`def:subfields-kappa` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-208`,
   114	whose paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502`.
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable abbrev kappa {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Semiring K]
   117	    [Algebra F K] [Finite ι]
   118	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K ≃ₗ[F] (ι → F) :=
   119	  b.equivFun
   120	
   121	/--
   122	Multiplication by `a` in basis coordinates, using Mathlib's
   123	`Algebra.leftMulMatrix`.  It is the multiplication table `K_a` in
   124	`def:subfields-kappa` (blueprint lines 196-199; paper
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable abbrev multiplicationTable {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F]
   128	    [Semiring K] [Algebra F K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   129	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K →ₐ[F] Matrix ι ι F :=
   130	  Algebra.leftMulMatrix b
   131	
   132	/--
   133	The finite-field trace used by the Pauli phases.  This is a thin wrapper around
   134	Mathlib's basis-independent `Algebra.trace`, matching `def:subfield-trace` and
   135	Equation `eq:def-trace` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`
   136	(`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   137	-/
   138	noncomputable abbrev binTrace (K : Type*) [CommRing K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] :
   139	    K →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2 :=
   140	  Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K
   141	
   142	/-- The trace selected by a fixed model; this is the map denoted `tr` in the
   143	paper's `def:binary-representation`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`,
   144	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`. -/
   145	noncomputable def fixedBinTrace {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K → ZMod 2 :=
   146	  binTrace F.K
   147	
   148	/--
   149	The matrix-trace presentation of `fixedBinTrace`, a statement-level bridge to
   150	Equation `eq:def-trace`.  It is the trace assertion in `def:subfield-trace`,
   151	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.  Mathlib's
   153	`Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` supplies the basis-independent equality.
   154	-/
   155	theorem fixedBinTrace_eq_matrixTrace {q ι : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q)
   156	    (b : Module.Basis (Fin ι) (ZMod 2) F.K) (a : F.K) :
   157	    fixedBinTrace F a = (multiplicationTable b a).trace := by
   158	  exact Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace b a
   159	
   160	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/--
   120	Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
   121	This is `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, equations `eq:pauli-obs-proj` and
   122	`eq:pauli-inversion-0`, in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`;
   123	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   124	Both directions are deliberately left as proof-level obligations in stage 4.1.
   125	-/
   126	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   127	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   128	    tauObservable W a =
   129	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   130	  sorry
   131	
   132	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   133	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   134	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   136	-/
   137	theorem pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
   139	    pauliProj W e =
   140	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   141	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by
   142	  sorry
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Subspaces
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:433-492`.
    14	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    22	
    23	/--
    24	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    25	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`;
    26	paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    28	-/
    29	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    30	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    31	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    32	
    33	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    34	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    36	-/
    37	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    38	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    39	  Pi.single i 1
    40	
    41	/--
    42	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    43	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    45	-/
    46	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    47	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    48	
    49	/--
    50	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    51	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`; paper origin
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    53	-/
    54	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    55	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    56	
    57	/--
    58	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    59	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:455-466`,
    60	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    61	-/
    62	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    63	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    64	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    65	  sorry
    66	
    67	/--
    68	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    69	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    70	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    71	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`; paper origin
    72	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    73	-/
    74	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    75	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    76	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))
    77	
    78	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the
    79	canonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/
    80	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`.
    83	-/
    84	noncomputable def lineRep {m : ℕ}
    85	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
    86	  lineRepMap v u
    87	
    88	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
     2	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    14	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
    15	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
    16	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	
    25	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    26	
    27	/--
    28	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    29	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    30	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    31	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    32	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    33	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    34	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    35	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    36	-/
    37	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    38	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    39	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    40	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    41	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    42	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    43	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    44	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    45	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    46	
    47	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    48	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    49	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    51	-/
    52	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    53	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    54	
    55	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    56	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    58	-/
    59	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    60	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    61	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    62	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    63	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    64	      fun x =>
    65	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    66	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    67	
    68	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    69	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    72	-/
    73	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    74	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    75	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    76	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    77	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    78	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    79	
    80	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    81	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    82	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    84	-/
    85	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    86	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    87	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    88	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    89	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    90	
    91	/--
    92	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    93	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    95	-/
    96	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    97	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
    98	
    99	/--
   100	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   101	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   102	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   104	-/
   105	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   106	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   107	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   108	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   109	
   110	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   111	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   112	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   113	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   114	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   116	-/
   117	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   118	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   119	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   120	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   121	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   122	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   123	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   124	
   125	/--
   126	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   127	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, with
   128	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   129	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the
   130	level proof remains deferred in this skeleton.
   131	-/
   132	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   133	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   134	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   135	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   136	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   137	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   138	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   139	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   140	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   141	  sorry
   142	
   143	/--
   144	The graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge
   145	`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
   146	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
   147	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   148	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   149	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   150	-/
   151	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   152	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   153	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   154	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   155	
   156	/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
   157	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   158	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   159	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   160	  sorry
   161	
   162	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    49	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    50	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    51	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    52	-/
    53	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    54	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    55	
    56	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    57	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    58	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    60	-/
    61	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    62	
    63	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	inductive LdType where
    68	  | point
    69	  | aline
    70	  | dline
    71	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    72	
    73	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    74	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    76	-/
    77	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    78	
    79	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    84	
    85	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    87	-/
    88	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    89	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    90	
    91	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    95	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    96	
    97	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   101	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   102	
   103	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   104	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   109	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   110	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   111	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   112	
   113	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   114	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   115	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   116	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   117	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   118	-/
   119	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   120	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   121	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   122	
   123	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   124	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   125	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   126	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   127	-/
   128	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   129	  fun i => match i with
   130	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   131	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   132	  | .inr _ => 0
   133	
   134	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   135	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   136	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   137	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   138	-/
   139	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   140	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   141	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   142	  fun i => match i with
   143	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   144	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   145	  | .inr _ => 0
   146	
   147	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   148	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   149	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   150	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   151	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   152	-/
   153	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   154	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   156	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   157	  fun i => match i with
   158	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   159	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   160	  | .inr j => direction j
   161	
   162	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   163	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   164	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   165	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   166	-/
   167	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   168	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   169	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   170	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   171	
   172	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   173	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   174	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   175	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   176	-/
   177	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   178	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   179	  sorry
   180	
   181	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   182	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   183	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   184	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   185	-/
   186	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   187	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   188	  sorry
   189	
   190	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   191	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   192	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   193	-/
   194	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   195	
   196	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   197	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   198	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   199	-/
   200	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   202	  Distribution.map
   203	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   204	    (fun s =>
   205	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   206	
   207	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   208	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   209	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   210	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   212	-/
   213	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   214	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   215	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  deriving DecidableEq
   218	
   219	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   220	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   221	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   222	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   223	-/
   224	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   225	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   226	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   228	
   229	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   230	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   235	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   236	  toFun
   237	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   238	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   239	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   240	  invFun
   241	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   242	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   243	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   244	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   245	  right_inv := by
   246	    intro x
   247	    cases x with
   248	    | inl a => rfl
   249	    | inr x =>
   250	        cases x with
   251	        | inl a => rfl
   252	        | inr a => rfl
   253	
   254	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   255	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   256	
   257	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   258	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   259	
   260	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   261	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   262	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   263	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   264	-/
   265	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   266	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   267	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   268	
   269	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   270	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   271	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   272	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   273	-/
   274	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   275	  match t, a with
   276	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   277	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   278	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   279	  | _, _ => false
   280	
   281	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   282	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   283	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   284	-/
   285	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   286	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   287	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   288	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   289	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   290	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   291	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   292	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   293	
   294	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   295	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   296	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   297	-/
   298	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   299	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   300	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   301	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   302	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   303	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   304	
   305	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   306	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   307	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   311	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   312	  open Classical in
   313	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   314	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   315	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   316	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   317	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   318	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   319	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   320	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   321	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   322	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   323	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   324	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   325	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   326	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   328	      else false
   329	
   330	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   331	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   332	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   333	-/
   334	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   335	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   336	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   337	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   338	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   339	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   340	  μ_prob := by sorry
   341	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   342	
   343	end
   344	
   345	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.CondLinear
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs

     4	/-!
     5	# The Magic Square game
     6	
     7	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     8	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
     9	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    74	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    75	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    77	-/
    78	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    79	
    80	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    81	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    86	  toFun
    87	    | .triple β => .inl β
    88	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    89	  invFun
    90	    | .inl β => .triple β
    91	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    92	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    93	  right_inv := by
    94	    intro x
    95	    cases x <;> rfl
    96	
    97	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    98	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
    99	
   100	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   101	
   102	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   103	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   105	-/
   106	def msWinPredicate :
   107	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   108	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   109	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   110	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   111	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   112	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   113	      decide
   114	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   115	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   116	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   117	      decide
   118	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   119	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   120	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   121	
   122	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   123	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   124	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   125	-/
   126	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   127	  QuestionA := MsType
   128	  QuestionB := MsType
   129	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   130	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   131	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   132	  μ_prob := by sorry
   133	  decide := msWinPredicate
   134	
   135	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.FieldBasis
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Lines
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.CondLinear
     4	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    49	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    50	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    51	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    52	-/
    53	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    54	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    55	
    56	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    57	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    58	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    60	-/
    61	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    62	
    63	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	inductive LdType where
    68	  | point
    69	  | aline
    70	  | dline
    71	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    72	
    73	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    74	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    76	-/
    77	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    78	
    79	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    84	
    85	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    87	-/
    88	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    89	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    90	
    91	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    95	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    96	
    97	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   101	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   102	
   103	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   104	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   109	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   110	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   111	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   112	
   113	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   114	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   115	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   116	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   117	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   118	-/
   119	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   120	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   121	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   122	
   123	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   124	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   125	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   126	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   127	-/
   128	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   129	  fun i => match i with
   130	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   131	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   132	  | .inr _ => 0
   133	
   134	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   135	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   136	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   137	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   138	-/
   139	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   140	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   141	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   142	  fun i => match i with
   143	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   144	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   145	  | .inr _ => 0
   146	
   147	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   148	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   149	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint

   153	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   154	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)

   158	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   159	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   160	  | .inr j => direction j

190	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   191	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   192	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   194	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   195	
   196	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   197	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   198	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   199	-/
   200	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   202	  Distribution.map
   203	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   204	    (fun s =>
   205	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   206	
   207	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   208	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   209	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   210	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   212	-/
   213	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   214	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   215	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  deriving DecidableEq
   218	
   219	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   220	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   221	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   222	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   223	-/
   224	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   225	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   226	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   228	
   229	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   230	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   235	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   236	  toFun
   237	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   238	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   239	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   240	  invFun
   241	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   242	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   243	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   244	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   245	  right_inv := by
   246	    intro x
   247	    cases x with
   248	    | inl a => rfl
   249	    | inr x =>
   250	        cases x with
   251	        | inl a => rfl
   252	        | inr a => rfl
   253	
   254	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   255	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   256	
   257	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   258	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   259	
   260	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   261	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   262	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   263	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   264	-/
   265	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   266	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   267	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   268	
   269	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   270	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   271	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   272	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   273	-/
   274	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   275	  match t, a with
   276	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   277	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   278	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   279	  | _, _ => false
   280	
   281	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   282	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   283	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   284	-/
   285	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   286	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   287	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   288	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   289	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   290	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   291	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   292	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   293	
   294	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   295	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   296	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   297	-/
   298	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   299	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   300	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   301	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   302	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   303	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   304	
   305	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   306	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   307	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   311	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   312	  open Classical in
   313	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   314	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   315	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   316	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   317	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   318	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   319	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   320	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   321	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   322	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   323	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   324	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   325	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   326	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   328	      else false
   329	
   330	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   331	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   332	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   333	-/
   334	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   335	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   336	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   337	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   338	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   339	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   340	  μ_prob := by sorry
   341	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   342	
   343	end
   344

     4	# Pauli basis test soundness
     5	
     6	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     7	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     8	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
     9	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    16	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    18	-/

    29	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    30	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    31	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    32	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    33	-/
    34	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    35	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    36	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    37	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    38	
    39	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    40	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    41	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    42	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    47	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    48	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    49	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    50	  U * M * Uᴴ
    51	
    52	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    53	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    54	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    55	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    58	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    59	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    60	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    61	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    62	
    63	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    64	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    65	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    66	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    70	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    72	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    73	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    74	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    75	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    76	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    77	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    78	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    79	    (fun p =>
    80	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    81	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    82	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    83	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    84	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    85	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    86	
    87	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    88	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    89	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    93	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    96	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    97	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    98	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    99	    (fun p =>
   100	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   101	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   102	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   103	
   104	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   105	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   107	-/
   108	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   109	  (.pauli W, 0)
   110	
   111	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   112	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   113	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   127	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   131	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   133	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   134	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   135	  fun p q =>
   136	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   137	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   138	    else 0
   139	
   140	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   141	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   142	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   145	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   146	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   147	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   148	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   149	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   150	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   151	  fun p q =>
   152	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   153	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   154	    else 0
   155	
   156	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   157	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   158	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   159	-/
   160	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   161	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   162	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   163	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   164	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   165	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   166	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   167	  fun p q =>
   168	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   169	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   170	    else 0
