   172	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   173	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   174	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   175	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   177	-/
   178	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   179	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   180	  ιA' : Type
   181	  ιB' : Type
   182	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   183	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   184	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   185	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   186	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   187	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   188	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   189	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   190	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   191	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   192	
   193	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   194	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   195	
   196	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   197	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   198	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   199	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   202	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   203	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   204	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   205	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   206	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   207	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   208	
   209	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   210	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   212	-/
   213	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   214	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   215	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   216	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   217	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   218	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   219	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   220	
   221	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   222	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   223	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   224	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   225	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   226	Blueprint
   227	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   228	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   229	
   230	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   231	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   232	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   233	-/
   234	theorem pauli_soundness :
   235	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   236	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   237	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   238	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   239	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   240	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   241	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   242	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   243	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   244	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   245	  sorry
   246	
   247	end

   431	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   432	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   433	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   434	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   435	-/
   436	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   437	  match t, a with
   438	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   439	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   440	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   441	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   442	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   443	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   444	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   445	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   446	  | _, _ => false
   447	
   448	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   449	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   453	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   454	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   455	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   456	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   457	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   458	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   459	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   461	
   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   475	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   477	-/
   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false

   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end
   584	
   585	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

220	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   221	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   222	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   223	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   224	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   225	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   226	-/
   227	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   228	  | .point _ => 1
   229	  | .aline _ => 2
   230	  | .dline _ => 3
   231	  | .pauli _ => 0
   232	  | .pairW _ => 1
   233	  | .pair => 1
   234	  | .ms _ => 1
   235	
   236	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   237	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   238	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   239	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   240	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   241	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   242	-/
   243	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   244	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   245	  match t with
   246	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   247	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   248	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   249	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   250	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   251	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   252	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   253	
   254	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   255	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   256	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   258	-/
   259	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   260	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   261	  sorry
   262	
   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   321	  by
   322	    classical
   323	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   324	    exact
   325	      Distribution.map
   326	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   327	        (fun s =>
   328	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   329	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   330	
   331	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   332	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   333	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   334	-/
   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq
   344	
   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   349	-/
   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   361	-/
   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   370	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   371	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   372	  invFun
   373	    | .inl a => .value a
   374	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   375	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   376	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   377	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   378	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   379	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   380	  left_inv := by
   381	    intro x
   382	    cases x <;> rfl
   383	  right_inv := by
   384	    intro x
   385	    cases x with
   386	    | inl a => rfl
   387	    | inr x =>
   388	        cases x with
   389	        | inl a => rfl
   390	        | inr x =>
   391	            cases x with
   392	            | inl a => rfl
   393	            | inr x =>
   394	                cases x with
   395	                | inl a => rfl
   396	                | inr x =>
   397	                    cases x with
   398	                    | inl a => rfl
   399	                    | inr x =>
   400	                        cases x with
   401	                        | inl a => rfl
   402	                        | inr a => rfl
   403	
   404	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   405	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   406	
   407	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   408	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   409	
   410	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   411	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   412	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   413	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   414	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   415	-/
   416	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   417	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   418	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   419	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   420	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   421	
   422	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   423	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   424	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   425	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   426	-/
   427	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   428	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   429	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)

     6	/-!
     7	# The Pauli basis test
     8	
     9	This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
    10	conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
    11	Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
    12	`Soundness.lean`.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:admissible`, `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
    17	and `def:pauli-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-367`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is `def:admissible` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    36	-/
    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	
    45	/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
    46	the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    49	-/
    50	theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
    51	  sorry
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
    54	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    55	quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
    56	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
    62	a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
    63	hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    66	-/
    67	def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    68	  q := P.q
    69	  m := P.m
    70	  d := P.d
    71	  k := 1
    72	  hm := P.one_le_m
    73	  hd := P.hd
    74	  hk := by decide
    75	  hq := P.hq
    76	  hdvd := P.hdvd
    77	
    78	/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter package.  It is
    79	the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
    80	`def:admissible`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    83	-/
    84	abbrev PauliScalar (P : AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K
    85	
    86	/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
    87	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
    88	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
    89	-/
    90	inductive PauliType where
    91	  | point (W : PauliKind)
    92	  | aline (W : PauliKind)
    93	  | dline (W : PauliKind)
    94	  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
    95	  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
    96	  | pair
    97	  | ms (t : MsType)
    98	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    99	
   100	/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the
   101	coordinates displayed in `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   102	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   104	-/
   105	abbrev PauliIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   106	  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)
   107	
   108	/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   109	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   111	-/
   112	abbrev PauliSpace (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliIndex P → PauliScalar P
   113	
   114	/-- The coefficient register indexed by the Boolean cube in
   115	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.
   117	-/
   118	abbrev PauliRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) := Cube P.m → PauliScalar P
   119	
   120	/- The nested sum is the fixed register order
   121	`V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
   122	/-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   123	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   124	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
   125	def pauliXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   126	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))
   127	
   128	/-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   129	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   130	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   131	-/
   132	def pauliZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   133	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))))
   134	
   135	/-- The scalar block `V_I` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   136	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   137	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   138	-/
   139	def pauliScalarBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   140	  z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ()))))
   141	
   142	/-- The direction block `V_V` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   143	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   144	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   145	-/
   146	def pauliDirectionBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   147	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))
   148	
   149	/-- The `r_X` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   150	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   151	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   152	-/
   153	def pauliRXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   154	  z (.inl (.inr ()))
   155	
   156	/-- The `r_Z` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   157	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   158	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   159	-/
   160	def pauliRZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   161	  z (.inr ())
   162	
   163	/-- Select the basis-dependent point block from a Pauli question content in
   164	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   165	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   166	-/
   167	def pauliPointBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   168	    Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   169	  match W with
   170	  | .X => pauliXBlock z
   171	  | .Z => pauliZBlock z
   172	
   173	/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli
   174	vector.  Lean-only coordinate plumbing for `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   175	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   177	-/
   178	def pauliToLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   179	    LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
   180	  fun i => match i with

180	  fun i => match i with
   181	  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
   182	  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
   183	  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j
   184	
   185	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   186	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing
   187	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   188	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   189	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   190	-/
   191	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   192	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
   193	  fun i => match i with
   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   195	      match W with
   196	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   197	      | .Z => 0
   198	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   199	      match W with
   200	      | .X => 0
   201	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   202	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   203	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   204	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   205	  | .inr _ => 0
   206	
   207	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
   208	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper

   236	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   237	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and

   251	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection

   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in

   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P

   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is

   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This

   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).

   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,

   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq

   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   370	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   371	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   372	  invFun
   373	    | .inl a => .value a
   374	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   375	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   376	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   377	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   378	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   379	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   380	  left_inv := by
   381	    intro x
   382	    cases x <;> rfl
   383	  right_inv := by
   384	    intro x
   385	    cases x with
   386	    | inl a => rfl
   387	    | inr x =>
   388	        cases x with
   389	        | inl a => rfl
   390	        | inr x =>
   391	            cases x with
   392	            | inl a => rfl
   393	            | inr x =>
   394	                cases x with
   395	                | inl a => rfl
   396	                | inr x =>
   397	                    cases x with
   398	                    | inl a => rfl
   399	                    | inr x =>
   400	                        cases x with
   401	                        | inl a => rfl
   402	                        | inr a => rfl

   404	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=

   410	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   411	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   412	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   413	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   414	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.

   416	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   417	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   418	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   419	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   420	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   421	
   422	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   423	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   424	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   425	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.

   427	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   428	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   429	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   430	
   431	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   432	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   433	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin

   436	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   437	  match t, a with
   438	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   439	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   440	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   441	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   442	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   443	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   444	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   445	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   446	  | _, _ => false
   447	
   448	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   449	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   452	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   453	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   454	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   455	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   456	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   457	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   458	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   459	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   461	
   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,

   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model

500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end

1	\chapter{Algebraic preliminaries for the Pauli basis test}
     2	\label{chap:qpbt-algebra}
     3	
     4	This chapter records the algebraic preliminaries needed for the quantum Pauli
     5	basis test, following the preliminaries of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}: subspace
     6	machinery over finite fields (which underlies the conditionally linear question
     7	distributions of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-games}), field extensions, traces, and
     8	self-dual bases, the low-degree code, lines in $\F_q^m$, and the generalized
     9	Pauli observables together with the EPR states they act on. Measurements,
    10	strategies, and consistency relations for nonlocal games are treated in
    11	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-games}; the test itself is defined in
    12	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
    13	
    14	\section{Linear spaces and subspaces}
    15	% Paper label sec:linear-spaces kept for cross-reference fidelity.
    16	\label{sec:linear-spaces}
    17	
    18	Linear spaces are always of the form $V = \F^n$ for a finite field $\F$ and an
    19	integer $n \ge 1$, unless explicitly stated otherwise. We write $\hat{E} =
    20	\{\hat{e}_1, \dots, \hat{e}_n\}$ for the standard basis of $V$, where
    21	$\hat{e}_i$ has a $1$ in the $i$-th coordinate and $0$'s elsewhere, and
    22	$\mathrm{End}(V)$ for the set of linear maps from $V$ to itself.
    23	
    24	\begin{definition}[Register subspace]\label{def:register-subspace}
    25		A \emph{register subspace} $S$ of $V$ is a subspace that is the span of a
    26		subset of the standard basis of $V$. Such a subspace is represented by an
    27		indicator vector $u \in \{0,1\}^s$, where $s = \dim(V)$, via
    28		$S = \mathrm{span}\{\hat{e}_i : u_i = 1\}$.
    29	\end{definition}
    30	
    31	\begin{definition}[Dot product and orthogonal subspace]\label{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    32		For two vectors $u = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \hat{e}_i$ and
    33		$v = \sum_{i=1}^n v_i \hat{e}_i$ in $V = \F^n$, the \emph{dot product} is
    34		\[
    35			u \cdot v = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i v_i \in \F\;.
    36		\]
    37		For a subspace $S$ of $V$, the \emph{subspace orthogonal to $S$ in $V$} is
    38		\[
    39			S^\perp = \bigl\{ u \in V : u \cdot v = 0 \text{ for all } v \in S \bigr\}\;.
    40		\]
    41		The notation $S^\perp$ leaves the ambient space $V$ implicit.
    42	\end{definition}
    43	
    44	Over finite fields, orthogonality lacks some of the familiar properties it has
    45	over $\R$ or $\C$; for example, a nonzero subspace may be orthogonal to itself,
    46	as is $\mathrm{span}\{(1,1)\}$ over $\F_2$. The following dimension identity
    47	nevertheless holds over every field.
    48	
    49	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:perp_perp}
    50		\uses{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    51		Let $S$ be a subspace of $V$. Then $\dim(S) + \dim(S^\perp) = \dim(V)$, and
    52		\[
    53			(S^\perp)^\perp = S\;.
    54		\]
    55	\end{lemma}
    56	\begin{proof}
    57		\uses{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    58		The elements of $S^\perp$ are the solutions of a feasible linear system whose
    59		coefficient matrix has $\dim(S)$ linearly independent rows, so the solution
    60		space has dimension exactly $\dim(V) - \dim(S)$. Every $u \in S$ is
    61		orthogonal to every element of $S^\perp$, so $S \subseteq (S^\perp)^\perp$.
    62		Applying the dimension identity twice shows that
    63		$\dim\bigl((S^\perp)^\perp\bigr) = \dim(S)$, so the inclusion is an equality.
    64	\end{proof}
    65	
    66	\begin{definition}[Complementary subspaces]\label{def:complementary}
    67		Two subspaces $S$ and $T$ of a linear space $V$ form a pair of
    68		\emph{complementary subspaces} of $V$ if
    69		\[
    70			S \cap T = \{0\}\;, \qquad S + T = V\;.
    71		\]
    72		In this case we write $V = S \oplus T$. Every $x \in V$ can be written
    73		uniquely as $x = x^S + x^T$ with $x^S \in S$ and $x^T \in T$; we call $x^S$
    74		(resp.\ $x^T$) the \emph{projection of $x$ onto $S$ parallel to $T$} (resp.\
    75		onto $T$ parallel to $S$). The unique linear map $L : V \to V$ with
    76		$x \mapsto x^S$ is the \emph{projector onto $S$ parallel to $T$}.
    77	\end{definition}
    78	
    79	A subspace may have many complementary subspaces: in $\F_2^2$, the subspace
    80	$S = \mathrm{span}\{(1,1)\}$ has the distinct complements
    81	$\mathrm{span}\{(1,0)\}$ and $\mathrm{span}\{(0,1)\}$. Given a basis of $S$,
    82	one may nevertheless single out a \emph{canonical} complement.
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Canonical complement]\label{def:canonical-complement}
    85		\uses{def:register-subspace}
    86		Let $\hat{E}$ be the standard basis of $V = \F^n$ and let
    87		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subset V$ be a set of $m$ linearly independent
    88		vectors. Write $v_i = \sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,j}\, \hat{e}_j$, and, using a
    89		canonical Gaussian-elimination algorithm valid over arbitrary fields,
    90		transform the $m \times n$ matrix $(a_{i,j})$ to reduced row echelon form
    91		$(b_{i,j})$. Let $J$ be the set of $m$ column indices containing the leading
    92		$1$ entry of each row of $(b_{i,j})$. The \emph{canonical complement of $F$}
    93		is the set of $n - m$ standard basis vectors
    94		\[
    95			F^\perp = \{\hat{e}_j : j \notin J\}\;.
    96		\]
    97		The canonical complement is a \emph{set} of vectors, not a subspace.
    98		% Basis-independence made explicit here: the source defines F^perp through
    99		% a basis but does not assert dependence on it; uniqueness of the reduced
   100		% row echelon form gives dependence on span(F) alone.
   101		Although defined through the basis $F$, it depends only on
   102		$\mathrm{span}(F)$ and the ambient standard basis: two bases of the same
   103		subspace form the rows of row-equivalent matrices, which have the same
   104		reduced row echelon form and hence the same pivot set $J$. The presentation
   105		through Gaussian elimination, adopted by \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, makes the
   106		canonical complement efficiently computable. If $S$ is a register subspace
   107		spanned by $\hat{E}_0 \subseteq \hat{E}$, then the canonical complement of
   108		$\hat{E}_0$ is $\hat{E} \setminus \hat{E}_0$, and its span coincides with
   109		$S^\perp$.
   110	\end{definition}
   111	
   112	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:canonical-complement}
   113		\uses{def:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   114		Let $S$ be the span of linearly independent vectors
   115		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subseteq V$, let $F^\perp$ be the canonical
   116		complement of $F$, and let $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$. Then
   117		\[
   118			S + T = V\;, \qquad S \cap T = \{0\}\;.
   119		\]
   120	\end{lemma}
   121	\begin{proof}
   122		\uses{def:canonical-complement}
   123		Let $A = (a_{i,j})$ be the $m \times n$ matrix whose rows are the $v_i$ and
   124		write $A = UB$ with $U$ invertible and $B$ in reduced row echelon form, so
   125		that the rows of $B$ are linearly independent and span $S$. The restrictions
   126		of the rows of $B$ to the columns in $J$ are still linearly independent and
   127		span $\F^m$, so for every $u \in V$ there is $v \in S$ that agrees with $u$
   128		on the coordinates in $J$. The difference $u - v$ is then supported on the
   129		coordinates outside $J$, that is, $u - v \in T$, which proves $S + T = V$.
   130		Counting dimensions forces $S \cap T = \{0\}$.
   131	\end{proof}
   132	
   133	\begin{definition}[Canonical linear map with prescribed kernel]\label{def:cl-canonical}
   134		\uses{def:canonical-complement, lem:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   135		Let $F \subseteq V$ be a set of linearly independent vectors and let
   136		$F^\perp$ be its canonical complement. The \emph{canonical linear map
   137		$L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ with kernel basis $F$} is the projector onto $T$
   138		parallel to $S$, where $S = \mathrm{span}(F)$ and
   139		$T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$; this is well defined by
   140		Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-complement}. Since the canonical complement
   141		depends only on $\mathrm{span}(F)$
   142		(Definition~\ref{def:canonical-complement}), so does $L$, and we also call
   143		it the \emph{canonical linear map with kernel $S$}. Note that
   144		$\ker(L) = S$.
   145	\end{definition}
   146	
   147	\begin{definition}[The map $L^\perp$]\label{def:Lperp}
   148		\uses{def:cl-canonical, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   149		Let $L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ be a linear map and let $F$ be a basis for
   150		$\ker(L)^\perp$. Define $L^\perp : V \to V$ as the canonical linear map with
   151		kernel basis $F$. (By the basis-independence noted in
   152		Definition~\ref{def:canonical-complement}, the map $L^\perp$ depends only
   153		on $\ker(L)$ and not on the chosen basis $F$.)
   154	\end{definition}
   155	
   156	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L_perp_perp}
   157		\uses{def:Lperp}
   158		Let $L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ be a linear map, $F$ a basis for
   159		$\ker(L)^\perp$, and $L^\perp$ as in Definition~\ref{def:Lperp}. Then
   160		$\ker(L^\perp) = \ker(L)^\perp$.
   161	\end{lemma}
   162	\begin{proof}
   163		\uses{def:Lperp, def:cl-canonical, lem:canonical-complement}
   164		Set $S = \mathrm{span}(F) = \ker(L)^\perp$ and $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$;
   165		by Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-complement} every $v \in V$ decomposes uniquely
   166		as $v = v^S + v^T$, and by definition $L^\perp v = v^T$. If
   167		$L^\perp v = 0$ then $v = v^S \in S = \ker(L)^\perp$. Conversely, if
   168		$v \in S$ then $v^T = 0$, so $L^\perp v = 0$.
   169	\end{proof}

   171	\section{Finite fields, traces, and self-dual bases}
   172	% Paper labels sec:finite-fields, sec:subfields, sec:ff-representations kept
   173	% for cross-reference fidelity.
   174	\label{sec:finite-fields}
   175	\label{sec:subfields}
   176	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   177	
   178	Let $p$ be a prime and $q = p^k$ a prime power. We write $\F_p$ and $\F_q$ for
   179	the finite fields with $p$ and $q$ elements; $p$ is the characteristic of
   180	$\F_q$, and $\F_p$ is its prime subfield.
   181	
   182	\begin{definition}[Coordinate map and multiplication tables]\label{def:subfields-kappa}
   183		% The source lets k range over all integers; the extension field exists
   184		% only for k >= 1, so that domain condition is made explicit here.
   185		Let $q$ be a prime power and $k \ge 1$ an integer, so that $\F_q$ is a
   186		subfield of $\F_{q^k}$ and $\F_{q^k}$ is a linear space of dimension $k$
   187		over $\F_q$.
   188		Fix a basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$. The bijection
   189		$\kappa_q : \F_{q^k} \to \F_q^k$ associated with this basis is
   190		\[
   191			\kappa_q : a \mapsto (a_i)_{i=1}^k\;, \qquad
   192			\text{where } a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i\;.
   193		\]
   194		The map $\kappa_q$ is an isomorphism of $\F_q$-vector spaces; in particular
   195		$\kappa_q(a + b) = \kappa_q(a) + \kappa_q(b)$ for all $a, b \in \F_{q^k}$.
   196		Moreover, multiplication by a fixed element corresponds to a linear map:
   197		for every $a \in \F_{q^k}$ there is a matrix $K_a \in \Mat_k(\F_q)$, the
   198		\emph{multiplication table of $a$ with respect to $\{e_i\}$}, such that
   199		$\kappa_q(ab) = K_a\, \kappa_q(b)$ for all $b \in \F_{q^k}$.
   200		The map extends coordinatewise to vectors, matrices, and sets: for
   201		$v = (v_1, \dots, v_n) \in \F_{q^k}^n$ set
   202		$\kappa_q(v) = (\kappa_q(v_i))_{i=1}^n \in \F_q^{kn}$; for
   203		$M = (M_{i,j}) \in \Mat_{m,n}(\F_{q^k})$ let
   204		$\chi_q(M) \in \Mat_{mk,nk}(\F_q)$ be the block matrix whose $(i,j)$-th
   205		block is $K_{M_{i,j}}$; and for a set $S$ of vectors put
   206		$\kappa_q(S) = \{\kappa_q(v) : v \in S\}$. When $q = p$ is the field
   207		characteristic, the subscript is omitted and we write $\kappa$ and $\chi$.
   208	\end{definition}
   209	
   210	\begin{definition}[Admissible field size]\label{def:admissible-size}
   211		A field size $q$ is \emph{admissible} if $q = 2^k$ for an odd integer $k$.
   212	\end{definition}
   213	
   214	Only fields $\F_{2^k}$ with $k$ odd are used in the analysis of the Pauli basis
   215	test.
   216	
   217	\begin{definition}[Trace of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$]\label{def:subfield-trace}
   218		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:admissible-size}
   219		The \emph{trace of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$} is the map
   220		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.

220		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   221		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-trace}
   222			\tr_{q^k \to q} : a \mapsto \Tr(K_a)
   223		\end{equation}
   224		for $a \in \F_{q^k}$, where $K_a$ is the multiplication table of $a$ with
   225		respect to the basis $\{e_i\}$. The trace is an $\F_q$-linear map from
   226		$\F_{q^k}$ to $\F_q$, and it is independent of the choice of basis, as can
   227		be seen from the equivalent formula
   228		\[
   229			\tr_{q^k \to q}(a) = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} a^{q^j}\;.
   230		\]
   231		For admissible $q = 2^k$ we use the shorthand $\tr$ for $\tr_{q \to 2}$.
   232	\end{definition}
   233	
   234	\begin{definition}[Dual, self-dual, and normal bases]\label{def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   235		\uses{def:subfield-trace}
   236		A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', \dots, e_k'\}$ of a basis
   237		$\{e_1, \dots, e_k\}$ of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$ is a basis such that
   238		$\tr_{q^k \to q}(e^{}_i e'_j) = \delta_{i,j}$ for all
   239		$i, j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$. A \emph{self-dual basis} is one equal to its own
   240		dual. If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set
   241		$\{\alpha^{q^j}\}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$, that
   242		basis is called a \emph{normal basis}. Self-dual and normal bases do not
   243		exist for every field extension, but for $q = 2$ and odd $k$ a self-dual
   244		normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ always exists; \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}
   245		exhibits one through an explicit construction.
   246	\end{definition}
   247	
   248	\begin{lemma}[Coordinate maps of self-dual bases]\label{lem:downsize_field}
   249		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace,
   250			def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   251		Let $q$ be a prime power, $k \ge 1$ an integer, and $\{e_i\}$ a self-dual
   252		basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$. The map $\kappa_q$ corresponding to
   253		$\{e_i\}$ satisfies:
   254		\begin{enumerate}
   255			\item for all $x \in \F_{q^k}$,
   256			      $\kappa_q(x) = \bigl(\tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_1), \dots,
   257			      \tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_k)\bigr)$;
   258			\item for all $x, y \in \F_{q^k}$,
   259			      $\tr_{q^k \to q}(xy) = \kappa_q(x) \cdot \kappa_q(y)$;
   260			\item for all $M \in \Mat_{m,n}(\F_{q^k})$ and $v \in \F_{q^k}^n$,
   261			      $\chi_q(M)\, \kappa_q(v) = \kappa_q(Mv)$.
   262		\end{enumerate}
   263		Items 1 and 2 use self-duality; item 3 holds for an arbitrary basis.
   264	\end{lemma}
   265	\begin{proof}
   266		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace, def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   267		For item 1, write $x = \sum_i x_i e_i$, multiply both sides by $e_j$, and
   268		take traces: $\tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_j) = \sum_i x_i \tr_{q^k \to q}(e_i e_j)
   269		= x_j$ by self-duality. For item 2, expand
   270		$xy = \sum_{i,j} x_i y_j e_i e_j$ and take traces; self-duality retains
   271		exactly the diagonal terms, giving $\sum_i x_i y_i = \kappa_q(x) \cdot
   272		\kappa_q(y)$. For item 3, the $i$-th block of $\kappa_q(Mv)$ equals
   273		$\sum_j \kappa_q(M_{i,j} v_j) = \sum_j K_{M_{i,j}}\, \kappa_q(v_j)$, which
   274		is the $i$-th block row of $\chi_q(M)$ applied to $\kappa_q(v)$.
   275	\end{proof}
   276	
   277	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:one}
   278		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace, def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   279		Let $k$ be an odd integer and $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ a self-dual normal basis of
   280		$\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$. Then $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i$, and the
   281		representation $\kappa(1)$ of the unit $1 \in \F_{2^k}$ is the all-ones
   282		vector in $\F_2^k$.
   283	\end{lemma}
   284	\begin{proof}
   285		\uses{lem:downsize_field}
   286		Normality gives $e_{i+1} = e_i^2$ (indices taken cyclically), and
   287		$\tr(b^2) = \tr(b)$ for every $b \in \F_{2^k}$ because squaring permutes the
   288		terms of $\tr(b) = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} b^{2^j}$, using $b^{2^k} = b$. Hence all
   289		the values $\tr(e_i)$ coincide. If the common value were $0$, then $\tr$
   290		would vanish identically on $\F_{2^k}$ by linearity; but then item 1 of
   291		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} would give $\kappa(b) =
   292		(\tr(b e_1), \dots, \tr(b e_k)) = 0$ for every $b$, contradicting the
   293		bijectivity of $\kappa$. Thus $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i$, and item 1 of
   294		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   295		$\kappa(1) = (\tr(e_1), \dots, \tr(e_k)) = (1, \dots, 1)$.
   296	\end{proof}
   297	
   298	\begin{definition}[Binary representation of field elements]\label{def:binary-representation}
   299		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:admissible-size,
   300			def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   301		Let $q = 2^k$ be an admissible field size. For each odd $k$ we fix, once and
   302		for all, a self-dual normal basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{2^k}$ over
   303		$\F_2$ together with its multiplication tables
   304		$\{K_{e_i}\}_{i=1}^k$ (Definition~\ref{def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis});
   305		the maps $\kappa$ and $\tr$ always refer to this basis. The \emph{binary
   306		representation} of $a \in \F_{2^k}$ is the $k$-bit string
   307		$\kappa(a) \in \F_2^k$, the \emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}; the two are
   308		freely identified. Addition of representations is bitwise addition modulo
   309		$2$, and multiplication is determined by the multiplication tables through
   310		\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-mult}
   311			\kappa(ab) = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i\, \kappa(e_i b)
   312			= \sum_{i=1}^k a_i \bigl(K_{e_i}\, \kappa(b)\bigr)\;,
   313		\end{equation}
   314		where $\kappa(a) = (a_i)_{i=1}^k$.
   315	\end{definition}

   317	\section{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   318	% Paper label sec:ld-encoding kept for cross-reference fidelity.
   319	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   320	
   321	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree]\label{def:polynomials-degree}
   322		\uses{def:polyfunc}
   323		An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   324		\[
   325			f(x_1, \dots, x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m}
   326			c_\alpha\, x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   327		\]
   328		with coefficients $c_\alpha \in \F_q$; the coefficients are uniquely
   329		determined by $f$, since the $q^m$ monomial functions indexed by
   330		$\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m$ span the $q^m$-dimensional space of all
   331		functions $\F_q^m \to \F_q$ and are therefore linearly independent. The
   332		polynomial $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if
   333		$c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when $\alpha_i \le d$ for all $1 \le i \le m$, and
   334		\emph{total degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when
   335		$\sum_i \alpha_i \le d$. (Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are those
   336		of individual degree $1$.
   337		% Relationship to def:polyfunc: polyfunc keeps polynomial representatives,
   338		% so evaluation identifies it with the function classes above only for
   339		% d <= q-1.
   340		Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc} introduces the set $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ of
   341		polynomials in $\F_q[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ of degree at most $d$ in each
   342		variable, identified by their polynomial representatives rather than by the
   343		functions they induce. Evaluation maps $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ onto the set of
   344		$m$-variate polynomials of individual degree at most $\min(d, q-1)$ in the
   345		sense above; for $d \le q-1$ this map is a bijection, while for $d \ge q$
   346		distinct representatives, such as $x_1^q$ and $x_1$, induce the same
   347		function. Statements phrased in terms of $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ retain the
   348		representative convention of Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}.
   349	\end{definition}
   350	
   351	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz--Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]\label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   352		% Restatement of lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree under the source's label.
   353		\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
   354		Let $f, g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials of total degree at
   355		most $d$. Then
   356		\[
   357			\Prb_{\bx \sim \F_q^m}[f(\bx) = g(\bx)] \le \frac{d}{q}\;.
   358		\]
   359	\end{lemma}
   360	\begin{proof}
   361		\uses{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   362		This is Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}, stated and proved in
   363		Chapter~\ref{chap:preliminaries}; it is restated here under the label used
   364		by \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   365	\end{proof}
   366	
   367	\begin{remark}\label{rem:schwartz-zippel-restated}
   368		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel} restates the total-degree bound of
   369		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} under the label used by
   370		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The individual-degree consequence,
   371		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-individual}, shows that distinct elements of
   372		$\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ agree on at most an $md/q$ fraction of the points of
   373		$\F_q^m$; the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses the bound in this
   374		individual-degree form.
   375	\end{remark}
   376	
   377	The Schwartz--Zippel lemma implies that low-degree polynomials form an
   378	error-correcting code with good distance, the \emph{low-degree code} (a special
   379	case of the generalized Reed--Muller code).
   380	
   381	\begin{definition}[Low-degree encoding]\label{def:low-degree-encoding}
   382		\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
   383		Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$. For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   384		define the $m$-variate multilinear polynomial over $\F_q$
   385		\[
   386			\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)
   387			= \prod_{i : y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i : y_i = 0} (1 - x_i)\;,
   388		\]
   389		identifying $\{0,1\}$ with a subset of $\F_q$. Restricted to the subcube
   390		$\{0,1\}^m$, the polynomial $\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}$ vanishes everywhere except
   391		at $x = y$, where it equals $1$. For $a \in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates
   392		of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ (identifying $\{0,1\}^m$ with
   393		$\{1, \dots, M\}$ by the lexicographic ordering). The \emph{low-degree
   394		encoding of $a$} is the multilinear polynomial $g_a : \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   395		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   396		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   397			g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\;.
   398		\end{equation}
   399		For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ one has $g_a(y) = a_y$, and $g_a$ has total
   400		degree at most $m$.
   401	\end{definition}
   402	
   403	\begin{definition}[Indicator vector and linearity of the encoding]\label{def:indicator-vector}
   404		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   405		For $x \in \F_q^m$, the \emph{indicator vector} is
   406		\[
   407			\mathrm{ind}_m(x)
   408			= \bigl(\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\bigr)_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \in \F_q^M\;.
   409		\]
   410		With this notation the low-degree encoding satisfies, for every
   411		$a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$,
   412		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   413		\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   414			g_a(x) = a \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)\;;
   415		\end{equation}
   416		in particular the map $a \mapsto g_a$ is $\F_q$-linear.
   417	\end{definition}
   418	
   419	Since encodings $g_a$ are multilinear, hence of total degree at most $m$, two
   420	encodings of distinct strings agree on at most an $m/q$ fraction of points of
   421	$\F_q^m$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel}.
   422	
   423	\begin{definition}[Decoding maps]\label{def:decoding-map}
   424		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding}
   425		For $H \subseteq \F_q$, the \emph{decoding map} $\mathrm{Dec}_H$ takes as
   426		input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and returns the vector
   427		$a \in \F_q^M$ defined by: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, set $a_y = g(y)$ if
   428		$g(y) \in H$, and $a_y = 0$ otherwise. For all $a \in H^M$ one has
   429		$\mathrm{Dec}_H(g_a) = a$. We write $\mathrm{Dec}(\cdot)$ for the boolean
   430		decoding map $\mathrm{Dec}_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.
   431	\end{definition}
